facts.statement: Prosaurolophus lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous period, approximately 75.7 to 74.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been found in the late Campanian-aged Dinosaur Park Formation in Alberta, and the roughly contemporaneous Two Medicine Formation in Montana, dating to around 75.7 to 74.1 million years ago.

facts.statement: The type species Prosaurolophus maximus was described by Barnum Brown in 1916.
facts.quote: The type species is P. maximus, described by American paleontologist Barnum Brown of the American Museum of Natural History in 1916.

facts.statement: A second species, P. blackfeetensis, was described by Jack Horner in 1992, though later research found it to be synonymous with P. maximus.
facts.quote: A second species, P. blackfeetensis, was described by Jack Horner of the Museum of the Rockies in 1992.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown recovered the first Prosaurolophus skull in 1915 from the Red Deer River in Alberta.
facts.quote: Well-known paleontologist Barnum Brown recovered a duckbill skull in 1915 for the American Museum of Natural History (AMNH 5836) from the Red Deer River of Alberta, near Steveville.

facts.statement: A nearly complete skeleton and skull of Prosaurolophus were described by William Parks in 1924.
facts.quote: one is a nearly complete skeleton and skull, described by William Parks in 1924.

facts.statement: Fossils of P. blackfeetensis were found in a bonebed in Glacier County, Montana.
facts.quote: This specimen, and the remains of three or four other individuals, were found in Glacier County, Montana.

facts.statement: Researchers interpret the Montana bonebed as evidence that Prosaurolophus congregated near water sources during droughts.
facts.quote: The bonebed is interpreted as reflecting a group of animals that congregated near a water source during a drought.

facts.statement: Prosaurolophus is characterized by a small, solid crest formed by nasal bones located in front of the eyes.
facts.quote: Its most recognizable feature is a small solid crest formed by the nasal bones, sticking up in front of the eyes.

facts.statement: The largest known specimen of Prosaurolophus had a skull 0.9 meters long, a body length of 8.5 meters, and a mass of 3 metric tons.
facts.quote: Prosaurolophus was a large-headed duckbill; the most complete described specimen has a skull around 0.9 m long with its body size measuring 8.5 m in length and 3 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: The crest grew proportionally throughout the animal's life, leading to speculation that it may have supported soft tissue structures like inflatable nasal sacs.
facts.quote: This crest grew isometrically (i.e. without changing in proportion) throughout the lifetime of the individual, leading to speculation that the species may have had a soft tissue display structure, such inflatable nasal sacs.

facts.statement: The relationship between Prosaurolophus and Saurolophus is debated, with some researchers finding them closely related while others place Prosaurolophus closer to Brachylophosaurus, Edmontosaurus, Gryposaurus, and Maiasaura.
facts.quote: However, this is contentious; some authors have found the animals to be closely related, whereas others have not, instead finding it closer to Brachylophosaurus, Edmontosaurus, Gryposaurus, and Maiasaura.

facts.statement: John Ostrom identified a "pseudonarial crest" as a unifying feature of Prosaurolophus, Brachylophosaurus, and Saurolophus, distinguishing them from lambeosaurines.
facts.quote: Ostrom found that the saurolophines Brachylophosaurus, Prosaurolophus, and Saurolophus all possessed a "pseudonarial crest", a feature which united them, while distinguishing them from hollow-crested lambeosaurines.

facts.statement: Brett-Surman classified Prosaurolophus and Saurolophus together in a group within Hadrosaurinae, distinct from the Edmontosaurus and Kritosaurus lineages.
facts.quote: Brett-Surman (1975) also followed Sternberg with sinking Saurolophinae into Hadrosaurinae, and like Hopson, he recognized three groups within the subfamily. Like Hopson, one group was called the Edmontosaurus lineage, the second the Kritosaurus group, and the third uniting Prosaurolophus and Saurolophus.

facts.statement: The second species Prosaurolophus blackfeetensis was described by Jack Horner in 1992.
facts.quote: Una segunda, Prosaurolophus blackfeetensis, lo fue por Jack Horner del Museo de las Rocosas en 1992.

facts.statement: Prosaurolophus lived during the late Cretaceous, approximately 75 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivieron a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 75 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Its most important feature is a small solid crest formed by nasal bones projecting upward in front of the eyes.
facts.quote: Su característica más importante es una pequeña cresta sólida formada por los huesos nasales, saliendo para arriba por delante de los ojos.

facts.statement: Remains suggest the animal reached a length of around 9 meters.
facts.quote: Los restos indicarían que alcanzaba alrededor de 9 metros de largo

facts.statement: Prosaurolophus maximus was the most common hadrosaurine in the upper section of the Dinosaur Park Formation, deposited about 75.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: It was the most common hadrosaurine of this section, which was deposited about 75.5 million years ago.

facts.statement: Prosaurolophus maximus likely acted as a browser, feeding on conifer trees and bark in coastal floodplains rather than grazing.
facts.quote: Prosaurolophus maximus itself lived in coastal floodplains fed on the conifer trees and the tree bark in the area, implying that it was more likely a browser rather than a grazer.

facts.statement: The bony facial crest and possibly nasal diverticula served as potential methods for social display.
facts.quote: The bony facial crest is an obvious candidate, and nasal diverticula may also have been present.

facts.statement: Inflatable soft-tissue sacs associated with the crest could have been used for both visual and auditory signals.
facts.quote: Such sacs could be used for both visual and auditory signals.

facts.statement: Prosaurolophus is classified within the subfamily Saurolophinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Saurolophinae

facts.statement: The genus authority is attributed to Brown, 1916.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Brown, 1916

facts.statement: The grouping of Prosaurolophus and Saurolophus has been problematic when trying to place them among hadrosaurines.
facts.quote: The Prosaurolophus-Saurolophus clade has been a problematic grouping when trying to place among hadrosaurines.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the clade is closer to Edmontosaurus due to numerous unifying features.
facts.quote: However, the clade might be closer to Edmontosaurus, as the features are more numerous uniting them.

facts.statement: The genus is known from nearly 25 individuals of the two species, including skulls and skeletons, though the remains remain confusing.
facts.quote: Es conocido por cerca de 25 individuos de las dos especies, que incluyen cráneos y esqueletos, pero aun así los restos son confusos.

facts.statement: The most complete described specimen of Prosaurolophus had a skull approximately 90 centimeters long and a total body length of 8.5 meters.
facts.quote: el ejemplar más completo descripto tenía un cráneo de alrededor de 90 centímetros y un largo total del cuerpo de 8,5 metros.

facts.statement: Prosaurolophus possessed a small, solid, triangular crest located on the forehead between the eyes, with concave sides forming depressions.
facts.quote: Este poseía una pequeña, maciza y triangular cresta en la frente, entre los ojos, los lados de la cresta eran cóncavos, formando unas depresiones.

facts.statement: Researchers speculate that the crest, which grew isometrically without changing proportions during the individual's life, may have supported soft tissue structures like inflatable nasal sacs for display.
facts.quote: Esta cresta creció isométricamente, es decir, sin cambiar en proporción, durante la vida del individuo, lo que llevó a la especulación de que la especie pudo haber tenido una estructura de exhibición de tejido blando, como sacos nasales inflables.

facts.statement: Like most hadrosaurs, Prosaurolophus had a flat front of the skull that widened rostrally to form a beak ideal for stripping leaves and branches from North American forests.
facts.quote: Como casi todos los hadrosáuridos, el frente del cráneo era plano y se ensanchaba rostralmente para formar un pico, ideal para arrancar las hojas y ramas de los bosques de Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The back of the mouth contained thousands of teeth ideal for grinding food before it was swallowed.
facts.quote: La parte posterior de la boca tenía millares de dientes ideales para desmenuzar el alimento antes de que fuera tragado.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Barnum Brown unearthed a skull in 1915 for the American Museum of Natural History, cataloged as AMNH 5836, from the Red Deer River in Alberta near Steveville.
facts.quote: El reconocido paleontólogo Barnum Brown desenterró un cráneo en 1915 para el Museo Americano de Historia Natural, AMNH 5836, del Río Red Deer en Alberta, cerca de Steveville.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown described the specimen in 1916 as a new genus, Prosaurolophus.
facts.quote: El mismo describió el espécimen en 1916 como un nuevo género, Prosaurolophus.

facts.statement: An almost complete skeleton and skull were discovered and described by William Parks in 1924.
facts.quote: uno de estos fue un esqueleto y un cráneo casi completos, descritos por William Parks en 1924.

facts.statement: The second species, P. blackfeetensis, is based on a specimen from the Museum of the Rockies, MOR 454, which was described by Jack Horner.
facts.quote: La segunda especie, P. blackfeetensis, está basada en un espécimen del Museo de las Rocosas, MOR 454, que fue descrito Jack Horner.

facts.statement: This specimen and the remains of three other individuals were found in Glacier County, Montana.
facts.quote: Este espécimen, y los restos de otros tres individuos, fueron encontrados en el Condado Glacier de Montana.

facts.statement: The bonebed is interpreted as evidence of a group of animals gathering near a water source during a drought.
facts.quote: El lecho se interpreta como reflejo de un grupo de animales que se juntaron cerca de una fuente de agua durante una sequía.

facts.statement: Recent studies have considered the differences between the two species insufficient to support them as distinct species.
facts.quote: Estudios más recientes han considerado las diferencias como insuficientes para sustentar dos especies.

facts.statement: Prosaurolophus lived in the forests of North America.
facts.quote: ideal para arrancar las hojas y ramas de los bosques de Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Prosaurolophus is a hadrosaurine duck-billed dinosaur characterized by lacking a hollow crest.
facts.quote: Como todo hadrosáurido hadrosaurino, se caracteriza por la falta de la creta hueca.

facts.statement: Charles Sternberg argued in 1954 that the subfamily Saurolophinae should be merged into Hadrosaurinae.
facts.quote: En 1954, Charles Sternberg revaluó los géneros en Hadrosauridae, invocando la probabilidad de que Saurolophinae se hundiera en Hadrosaurinae.

facts.statement: Friedrich von Huene separated Saurolophinae from Hadrosauridae and named it the family Saurolophidae.
facts.quote: Friedrich von Huene separó Saurolophinae de Hadrosauridae, nombrando Saurolophidae.

facts.statement: Horner and colleagues recovered Prosaurolophus as not closely related to Saurolophus in a 2004 phylogenetic analysis.
facts.quote: Horner y col. en 2004 también recuperaron una filogenia diferente de Saurolophinae. Prosaurolophus fue, por primera vez, recuperado separado de Saurolophus, de hecho, ni siquiera estaba estrechamente relacionado.

facts.statement: The Prosaurolophus-Saurolophus clade has been problematic to classify among hadrosaurines due to conflicting skull characteristics.
facts.quote: El clado Prosaurolophus-Saurolophus ha sido un grupo problemático al intentar ubicarlo entre los hadrosaurinos.

facts.statement: Weishampel and Horner conducted the first cladistic analysis covering Hadrosauridae relationships in 1990.
facts.quote: El primer análisis cladístico que abarcó las interrelaciones de Hadrosauridae fue realizado por Weishampel y Horner en 1990.

facts.statement: A 2004 cladogram by Horner, Weishampel, and Forster suggests Prosaurolophus is closely related to Gryposaurus.
facts.quote: El cladograma siguiente, está basado en el revisado por Jack Horner, David B. Weishampel y Catherine Forster en2004 para , para la segunda edición de The Dinosauria. Este muestra a Prosaurolophus más cercano a Gryposaurus, siendo solo uno de los tantas propuestas.

facts.statement: A detailed cladogram of hadrosaurid relationships was published in Acta Palaeontologica Polonica in 2013.
facts.quote: El Acta Palaeontologica Polonica publicó en 2013 un cladograma detallado de las relaciones de hadrosáuridos.

facts.statement: Prosaurolophus lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Prosaurolophus was a large herbivore with a sophisticated skull capable of mastication-like plant processing.
facts.quote: Como todo hadrosáurido, Prosaurolophus debió haber sido un gran herbívoro, comiendo plantas con un cráneo sofisticado que le permitiría un movimiento análogo a la masticación.

facts.statement: Prosaurolophus had continuously replaced and packed dental batteries containing hundreds of teeth, with only a few active at once.
facts.quote: Sus dientes fueron substituidos y empaquetados continuamente en las baterías dentales que juntaban centenares de dientes, aunque sólo un puñado de estos actuaba en un mismo momento.

facts.statement: Prosaurolophus fed on vegetation ranging from the ground up to approximately 4 meters in height.
facts.quote: La alimentación habría abarcado desde la tierra hasta alrededor de los 4 metros de altura.

facts.statement: Comparisons of scleral rings suggest Prosaurolophus may have been catemeral, active throughout the day with short rest intervals.
facts.quote: Las comparaciones entre los anillos esclerales de Prosaurolophus y las aves y reptiles modernos sugieren que puede haber sido catemeral, activo durante todo el día a intervalos cortos.

facts.statement: Prosaurolophus likely lived in groups for at least part of the year.
facts.quote: Como lo dicho más arriba, se sabe que estos animales habrían vivido en grupos, por lo menos en una parte del año.

facts.statement: Researchers hypothesize that nasal diverticula in Prosaurolophus were soft tissue sacs used for visual and auditory signaling.
facts.quote: Se postula que estos divertículos habrían tomado la forma de sacos inflables de tejido suave contenidos en las excavaciones profundas que flanquean la cresta y los agujeros para la nariz el S.

facts.statement: Earlier genera previously grouped with Prosaurolophus were later reclassified into Stephanosaurinae or Hadrosaurinae.
facts.quote: Los géneros anteriores se reclasificaron luego en Stephanosaurinae o Hadrosaurinae.

facts.statement: Charles Sternberg noted that the "hocked" ischium assigned to Saurolophus was not found with the holotype and was assigned based on locality alone.
facts.quote: Sternberg identificó que el isquion "con patas" asignado a Saurolophus no se encontró con el holotipo, y solo se le asignó debido a la ubicación del hallazgo.

facts.statement: William Parks discovered a complete Prosaurolophus skeleton in 1924 showing a "bare" ischium, suggesting Saurolophus likely lacked a hocked ischium.
facts.quote: William Parks en 1924 encontró un esqueleto completo de Prosaurolophus que muestra claramente un isquion "descalzo", lo que Sternberg se dio cuenta de que significaba que era poco probable que Saurolophus poseía un isquion "con patas".
